newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Dec 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Dec 26.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Thursday's edition of The Wall Street Journal:
- Few retailers are posting better than expected sales for the holiday shopping season.
- CalEnergy claimed control of Britain's Northern Electric after Northern's effort to derail the hostile $1.3 billion buyout bid fell short.
- Ford doubled the rebate on its 1977 Taurus to $1,000.
- Texaco agreed to sell its last petrochemicals plant to Huntsman for about $600 million.
- Bureaucrats at Japan's Finance Ministry appear poised to undermine efforts to break the ministry's hold on economic policy and curb its sway over the Bank of Japan.
- The FCC unveiled a proposal to overhaul the roughly $23 billion in fees local telephone companies collect each year to handle long-distance calls.
- Reebock sued Sony 's TriStar Pictures, claiming the studio violated a product-placement agreement for the Tom Cruise film "Jerry Maguire."
- WMX Technologies passed along a $25 percent raise to CEO Philip Rooney.
- Lockheed Martin agreed to pay $5.3 million to settle federal overcharge allegations.
- Stock prices rose in an abbreviated session Tuesday.
- Gold prices received a lift from heavy buying of jewelry by consumers during the holiday shopping season.
- Bradlees said Mark Cohen, chairman and CEO, resigned at the board's request.
- KCS Energy said it has agreed to give up a lucrative natural-gas supply contract to settle a suit brought by a unit of El Paso Energy.
- Gemstar said it signed a definitive agreement to acquire rival StarSight in a stock swap valued at $273 million.
- Treasury bonds barely moved Tuesday, as investors headed for the sidelines before Christmas.
- Norm Zadeh and a partner plan to revive the Money Manager Verified Ratings - once the nation's best-known investment contests - in 1997.
